blogs.title: Hawaii’s Long Shadow: Ninth Circuit Reaffirms Sweeping Presidential Power Under §1182(f) to Halt Refugee Admissions
blogs.description: The panel’s stay order treats Trump v. Hawaii as dispositive on the President’s authority to suspend refugee entries under 8 U.S.C. §1182(f), emphasizing that courts may not conduct a “searching inquiry” into presidential justifications. This post analyzes how Pacito cements Hawaii’s deferential framework, the interplay with the Refugee Act’s broader scheme, and what this means for future executive suspensions targeting discrete classes of noncitizens. It also explores how Nken’s stay factors are operationalized when national-security-inflected justifications are invoked and what limits—if any—remain on §1182(f) after this ruling.

blogs.title: Are Refugee Services Mandatory? The Ninth Circuit’s Split Reading of §1522 and Post-Chevron Statutory Interpretation
blogs.description: The majority signals that the government is unlikely to prevail on at least one APA claim because §1522 requires post-admission reception and placement services, directing reinstatement of cooperative agreements. Judge Lee dissents, framing §1522 as permissive authorization tethered to appropriations, not a mandate. This post dissects the competing textual readings—“authorized” provisions versus “shall…to the extent of available appropriations”—and situates the debate in the post-Chevron landscape, where courts resolve statutory meaning without deference. It assesses implications for federal obligations to refugees, potential circuit splits, and appropriations-law constraints.

blogs.title: A Stay That Orders Action: The Panel’s Unusual Remedial Crafting and What It Signals About Equitable Powers on Appeal
blogs.description: Even while staying the district court’s injunctions, the panel orders the government to reinstate cooperative agreements to ensure statutory services for already-admitted refugees. This post examines the doctrinal footing for tailoring stays with affirmative carveouts under Nken and appellate equitable authority, compares the order to recent “shadow docket” carveouts, and evaluates separation-of-powers concerns. It also considers how the court balanced alleged irreparable harms with statutory compliance, and what this hybrid remedy portends for future nationwide program suspensions paired with statutory backstops.

blogs.title: The APA, Interagency Roles, and Defunding by Fiat: Why State’s Termination of Resettlement Agreements Faces Headwinds
blogs.description: The order flags likely success for plaintiffs on at least one APA challenge tied to the refugee-services funding cutoffs and agreement terminations. This post explores the tension between State’s termination of cooperative agreements and ORR/HHS’s statutory duties under §1522, the use of a separate foreign-aid order to halt USRAP-related funding, and the government’s apparent lack of progress on a promised RFP. It analyzes possible APA defects—contrary to law, failure to consider statutory responsibilities, and disregard of reliance interests—and how §1523’s reporting and accountability provisions may sharpen judicial scrutiny of abrupt program rollbacks.
